newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria invites bids for sale of banks.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria invites bids for sale of banks.

text.p: Nigeria's Central Bank said on Friday it was re-offering six failed banks for sale following enquiries from the public.

The six -- Century Merchant Bank, First African Trust Bank, Mercantile Bank, North-South Bank, Premier Commercial Bank and Progress Bank -- were first offered for sale last year after efforts to revive them failed.
Foreign investors can now own 100 percent of any business in Nigerian except in a few areas such as defence, according to reforms of the enterprises laws last year.

Interested local and foreign investors are to deposit a non-refundable $1,000 application fee and provide information on their company, the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) quoted the central bank as saying.
Prospective buyers are to provide evidence that they have the funds to manage the targetted bank as well as the names of their audited accounts for the last three years, the report said.
In addition, the central bank said bidders should submit a list of their directors and shareholders.
Bids are to close on September 30.
The bank said those who qualified would receive bidding instructions thereafter and would be allowed eight weeks to submit them.

Nigeria's regulatory authorities have been prosecuting bank executives deemed to have been ruinined a quarter of the country's banks in a large scale fraud that pervaded the banking system in the late 1980s when the sector was deregulated.
